- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is rising, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to capture momentum.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak for 3–5 days.
- When sentiment swings from bullish to bearish, model lags in correction; delay forecast drop by 1–2 days and reduce slope.
- If model shows strong upward trend but sentiment is weak, apply mean reversion: cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high if sentiment drops below 0.5.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds model by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, assume momentum bias; increase forecast by 0.5–1% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 3-day moving average of true price as baseline for correction.
